author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New England Patriots receiver A.J. Brown will undergo additional evaluation after injuring an ankle in the season opener, leaving his availability for Week 2 uncertain.

Coach Mike Vrabel said Thursday that the team needed more test results before deciding whether Brown could play in New England’s next game. Brown was hurt early in the third quarter of the Patriots’ 13-10 loss at Seattle on Wednesday and did not return.

Brown finished the opener with three receptions for 26 yards. His exit reduced the options available to quarterback Drake Maye as Seattle erased New England’s early lead and completed its fourth-quarter comeback. The Patriots’ offense will now prepare with multiple contingencies while Brown’s recovery is assessed.

New England is scheduled to host Pittsburgh on September 20. The longer-than-usual gap following the Wednesday opener gives Brown additional treatment and recovery time, but the team had not announced a firm practice or game status in the source report. Injury designations later in the preparation week should provide a clearer indication of whether he can return.
dek: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said the receiver needs additional testing after leaving New England’s season-opening loss in Seattle.
headline: A.J. Brown’s Week 2 status uncertain after ankle injury
